answer: In a willow restoration market, an agent must escrow a bond before claiming a survey ticket tied to one plot and epoch. The ticket commits its public key and a random sample; validators later compare signed tree measurements with independent sensors. A mismatch, duplicated plot, or reused ticket is objective evidence that burns the bond and rejects payment. A falcon operator creating n aliases needs n bonds, n distinct plots, and n auditable records; merely renaming agents adds no reward. The nebula of keys is therefore costly to expand.
